output. The DC-coupled means are \SI{5.00727}{\volt},
\SI{9.02697}{\volt}, and \SI{15.0537}{\volt} at the
\SI{5}{\volt}, \SI{9}{\volt}, and \SI{15}{\volt} settings,
approximately \SI{0.145}{\percent}, \SI{0.300}{\percent}, and
\SI{0.358}{\percent} above their targets. These averages show that the output stayed close to its setpoint
without a load.
new:
With the connector unloaded, average VBUS remained close to the selected
output. The DC-coupled means were \SI{5.00727}{\volt},
\SI{9.02697}{\volt}, and \SI{15.0537}{\volt} at the
\SI{5}{\volt}, \SI{9}{\volt}, and \SI{15}{\volt} settings,
respectively. These values were approximately \SI{0.145}{\percent},
\SI{0.300}{\percent}, and \SI{0.358}{\percent} above their targets.
reason: Removes a repeated conclusion and connects the measurements to their errors.

old:
Secondary-winding heating and limited power increase were observed near
\SIrange{3.3}{3.6}{\ampere} at the secondary output. The winding was
suspected to limit further power increase. Output behavior was comparable
to V1, while the modified tank shifted the main heating concern to the
input bridge.
new:
Secondary-winding heating and limited power increase were observed near
\SIrange{3.3}{3.6}{\ampere} at the secondary output, and the winding was
suspected to limit further power increase. Output behavior was comparable
to V1. After the tank change, the main heating concern shifted to the
input bridge.
reason: Connects the observed limit to its suspected cause and separates the comparison from the later heating observation.
facts_preserved: Secondary current is not connector power; winding limitation remains suspected.

old:
Removing the USB-PD section while retaining secondary rectification gave
the V3 edge-card layout an estimated net volume reduction of approximately
\SI{8}{\percent}. This reduced-function estimate is not a complete USB-C
power-density result; external regulation and USB-PD remain necessary.
Replacement planar magnetics were not installed within the project, so
further reduction and higher sustained output were not demonstrated.
new:
The V3 edge-card layout retained secondary rectification and removed the
USB-PD section, giving an estimated net volume reduction of approximately
\SI{8}{\percent}. External regulation and USB-PD remain necessary for a
complete USB-C supply. Replacement planar magnetics were not installed
within the project, leaving further reduction and sustained output to be
assessed.
reason: States the design change, estimate and remaining development in a connected sequence.
facts_preserved: Estimate concerns the reduced-function layout; replacement magnetics were not installed and sustained output was not demonstrated.

old:
V3 was prepared as a slimmer edge-card layout with secondary rectification
and the USB-PD output section removed. The estimated net volume reduction
is approximately \SI{8}{\percent}. Replacement planar magnetics were
not installed within the available time. V3 reached the layout stage; its losses, temperatures,
and continuous output were not tested. Equivalent USB-C functionality requires the external output
stage to be included in the comparison.
new:
V3 was prepared as a slimmer edge-card layout with secondary rectification
retained and the USB-PD output section removed. The estimated net volume
reduction is approximately \SI{8}{\percent}. Replacement planar magnetics
were not installed within the available time, and V3 remained at the layout
stage. Its losses, temperatures, and continuous output were not tested. A
comparison with equivalent USB-C functionality requires the external output
stage to be included.
reason: Makes the retained rectification and unfinished layout status explicit in the conclusion.
facts_preserved: V3 was unbuilt and untested, estimate is approximately 8%, and external output stage is required for equivalent function.

old:
The key correction was to identify PA2 as half-bridge current rather than
output current. PA1--PA2 product-based output-power control was replaced by
PA1 voltage regulation, with PA2 retained for load classification and
diagnostics. Optional PA0 feed-forward caps PA10 duty.

Loaded and load-removal tests show the combined controller response.
The tests did not hold all other settings fixed while changing one feature,
so the contribution of each change was not measured. For
example, \texttt{MAXRATE} requests a \SI{20}{\micro\second} period;
the achieved period and jitter require measured timing.
new:
PA2 measures half-bridge current, so multiplying it by secondary voltage
was not a suitable output-power feedback signal. The product-based control
was replaced by PA1 secondary-voltage regulation, while PA2 was retained
for load classification and diagnostics. Optional PA0 feed-forward caps
PA10 duty as the sensed primary voltage rises.

Loaded and load-removal tests show the combined controller response. The
individual changes were not tested at fixed settings, so their separate
contributions remain unmeasured. For example, \texttt{MAXRATE} requests a
\SI{20}{\micro\second} period; the achieved period and jitter require
measured timing.
reason: Recasts the feedback correction as a measurement problem and resulting control choice, then connects the combined test to the timing still to be measured.
facts_preserved: PA2 is half-bridge current; PA1 regulates the secondary; PA0 feed-forward caps duty; the requested period is not measured.

old:
Voltage regulation, load classification, complete-cycle scheduling, and
no-load guarding addressed incorrect sensing interpretation, irregular pulses,
and excess charging. Measurement review also separated waveform ripple from
the spread of acquisition averages. Original readings give a maximum
calculated output of \SI{79.89}{\watt}. Further loading toward the
\SI{100}{\watt} objective requires temperature histories as well as electrical readings.

The remaining campaign must pair input/output power, capture ripple with
known coupling and bandwidth, follow identified temperatures to stabilization,
and record controller state during load and protection events.
new:
The control changes addressed the problems found during bring-up: PA1
voltage regulation replaced the incorrect power interpretation, complete-cycle
scheduling addressed irregular pulses, and no-load guarding limited charging
after load removal. Measurement review separated waveform ripple from the
spread of acquisition averages. The original readings give a maximum
calculated output of \SI{79.89}{\watt}; further loading toward the
\SI{100}{\watt} objective requires temperature histories alongside the
electrical readings.

The remaining tests must pair input and output power, capture ripple with
known coupling and bandwidth, follow identified temperatures to stabilization,
and record controller state during load and protection events.
reason: Connects each bring-up issue to the actual control change, then relates the measured output to the next tests.
facts_preserved: 79.89 W calculated point and 100 W objective retained; no separate performance improvement claimed.

old:
The voltage-control firmware combined continuous DMA acquisition,
fixed-carrier burst scheduling, direct secondary-voltage regulation,
loaded duty adjustment, startup precharge, and separate no-load behavior.
The current-sense interpretation was corrected to match the installed
hardware.

V2 integrated the MCU onto the converter board. Timer and ADC assignments
were adapted, and a flash settings journal, browser commands, and logging
were implemented. Browser calibration and editable reference-load settings
were then added to repeat the duty search for connected test loads. Carrier
frequency and dead time can be set together with output disabled, allowing
switching conditions to be varied without rebuilding the firmware. The four-layer circuit and layout are documented in
the schematic and PCB prints. Archived firmware and supporting software
are included with the thesis and have been checked in software.
Preliminary powered observations appear in \cref{sec:res-v2-testing};
powered tests of the later adjustable firmware and comparable power and
thermal-endurance measurements are still needed.
new:
The control firmware uses continuous DMA acquisition and fixed-carrier
burst scheduling to regulate the secondary voltage. Loaded duty adjustment,
startup precharge, and separate no-load behavior address the different
operating conditions. The current-sense interpretation was corrected to
match the installed hardware.

V2 integrated the MCU onto the converter board, requiring adapted timer and
ADC assignments. A flash settings journal, browser commands, and logging
were implemented. Browser calibration and editable reference-load settings
were then added to repeat the duty search for connected test loads. Carrier
frequency and dead time can be set together with output disabled, allowing
switching conditions to be varied without rebuilding the firmware. The four-layer circuit and layout are documented in
the schematic and PCB prints. Archived firmware and supporting software
are included with the thesis and have been checked in software.
Preliminary powered observations appear in \cref{sec:res-v2-testing};
powered tests of the later adjustable firmware and comparable power and
thermal-endurance measurements are still needed.
reason: Organizes control contributions around their operating roles and links the MCU integration to the peripheral remapping, while retaining the boundary of powered testing.
facts_preserved: DMA, burst, precharge, loaded and no-load control, physical reference loads, output-disabled settings, and untested later firmware retained.

old:
The persistent V2 input hotspot after diode replacement shows that the
complete current and thermal paths require review. The suspected
single-via restriction needs checking because narrow pad connections and
interlayer paths can still restrict current and heat flow despite a large copper pour.

Secondary-winding heating motivated transformer optimization, which was
not completed with an installed replacement set. Likewise, the V3 volume
reduction followed removal of the USB-PD section. A complete-system
power-density comparison must include the equivalent external output
functions.
new:
The V2 input hotspot persisted after diode replacement, so the current and
thermal paths around the bridge need further investigation. A possible
single-via connection between layers remains suspect: narrow pad connections
and interlayer paths can restrict current and heat flow despite a large
copper pour.

Secondary-winding heating motivated transformer optimization, but a
replacement set was not installed. The V3 layout reduced volume by removing
the USB-PD section, so a complete-system power-density comparison must also
include the equivalent external output functions.
reason: Links the failed diode replacement to the next physical inspection and explains why the V3 volume comparison needs the external output stage.
facts_preserved: Via cause remains suspected; replacement magnetics not installed; V3 removes USB-PD and retains a reduced-function estimate.

old:
V2 integrated the MCU, LMG2652 stage, isolated sensing, and MPQ4242 USB-C
circuit on a four-layer PCB, documented in \cref{sec:app-v2-oct27}.
Later bench tests removed the external series inductor and used
transformer leakage with approximately \SI{1.66}{\nano\farad}.
Lower half-bridge heating was reported after the tank and timing changes, while
input-bridge heating persisted. The thermal image was reported as a
\SI{95}{\watt} run, with no duration or thermal-equilibrium record. These
V2 observations cannot be compared quantitatively with the V1.0 measurements.

The revised plan retains \SI{100}{\watt} continuous as the target and
\SI{65}{\watt} continuous as the minimum \cite{projectOctoberPlan}.
No stabilized run of defined duration has verified these levels or
the earlier \SI{75}{\watt} milestone. The reported approximately
\SI{85}{\watt} V2 baseline requires an identified repeat, separate from
the \SI{79.89}{\watt} result above.
new:
V2 integrated the MCU, LMG2652 stage, isolated sensing, and MPQ4242 USB-C
circuit on a four-layer PCB, documented in \cref{sec:app-v2-oct27}.
The external series inductor was removed after heating, and the tank used
transformer leakage with approximately \SI{1.66}{\nano\farad}. Half-bridge
heating was reported to decrease after the tank and timing changes, while
input-bridge heating persisted. The thermal image was reported from a
\SI{95}{\watt} run; its duration and temperature history were not recorded,
and the V2 observations do not provide a quantitative comparison with V1.0.

The revised plan retains \SI{100}{\watt} continuous as the target and
\SI{65}{\watt} continuous as the minimum \cite{projectOctoberPlan}.
Defined-duration tests with temperature histories are still needed at these
levels and at the earlier \SI{75}{\watt} milestone. The reported
approximately \SI{85}{\watt} V2 baseline should be repeated with the board,
firmware, settings, power readings, and temperatures recorded together. It is
separate from the \SI{79.89}{\watt} V1.0 result above.
reason: Connects the inductor heating to the tank change and its observed thermal result, then states the continuous tests and records needed to repeat the V2 baseline.
facts_preserved: All numerical values and references retained; 95 W is the thermal-image run, no equilibrium or quantitative V1 comparison is claimed, and 85 W remains a reported V2 baseline.
